scale.source: CLDR RBNF hr renders 10^9 as "jedna milijarda" and 10^12 as "jedan bilijun": Croatian counts in the long scale.

group_mark.source: CLDR common/main/hr.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae), number symbols: the group symbol is a dot.

decimal_mark.source: CLDR common/main/hr.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae), number symbols: the decimal symbol is a comma.

space_groups.source: CLDR common/main/hr.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae), number symbols: the group symbol is a dot, not a space, so a space between digit strings separates two numbers.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: CLDR RBNF hr writes a plural scale word only after its count ("dvije tisuće", 2000). A plural scale word with no count names an amount, not a number.

scale_noun_agrees.source: CLDR RBNF hr %spellout-cardinal-masculine renders 10^6, 2 x 10^6, 5 x 10^6 and 21 x 10^6 as "jedan milijun", "dva milijuna", "pet milijuna", "dvadeset i jedan milijun": the scale noun takes the number and case its count governs. The count governs by its last word, so the singular also follows 21. The scale words of this lexicon are scale_numeral entries whose plural flag carries that agreement.

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR RBNF hr renders 21 as "dvadeset i jedan"; reading also accepts "i" left out.

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF hr renders 345 as "tristo četrdeset i pet": "i" joins the last part; reading also accepts it after the hundreds.

joiner_between_groups.source: Hrvatska Wikipedija, "Tisuću i jedna noć" (1001 Nights): "i" before the last part after the thousands; CLDR RBNF hr renders 1001 as "tisuću jedan", with no "i". Reading accepts both.

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF hr renders 1100 as "tisuću sto" and 1500 as "tisuću petsto": no joiner stands before a round hundred after the thousands.

hundred_counts_below_thousand.source: unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 (CLDR RBNF hr data), %spellout-cardinal, rendering of 2100: "dvije tisuće sto": the hundred after the thousands is the next group, so a hundred multiplier takes no count of a thousand or more.

compound_parts_by_role.source: compound_words is true, with the source quoted there: the compound number words it cites join cardinal and ordinal words and joiners only, so a fraction noun or a collective is no part of one ("petin|dvajset" is no split).

comma_between_classes.source: CLDR RBNF hr writes no comma between two classes (1001, 1100 and 1500 in the joiner settings above). No source opened shows a comma between two classes of one number, so a comma ends a number.

joiner_before_last_group.source: Hrvatska Wikipedija, "Tisuću i jedna noć" (1001 Nights): "i" before the last part after the thousands; CLDR RBNF hr renders 1001 as "tisuću jedan", with no "i". Reading accepts both.

ordinal_style.source: CLDR RBNF hr renders 21 in %spellout-ordinal-masculine as "dvadeset prvi": only the last word is ordinal.

compound_words.source: CLDR RBNF hr writes 2000th as one word ("dvotisućiti"). A word that is a sequence of number words reads as its parts.

bare_noun_counts_one.source: Croatian has no article, so a singular collective or fraction noun alone counts one: a paraphrase, with no page quote.

decimal_fractions.source: CLDR RBNF hr reads the decimals after "zarez" as a cardinal ("dva zarez pet"). A part word also names a decimal place: Hrvatski jezični portal, "tisućinka" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/follow-up-prs/sources/hr/hjp-tisućinka.txt): "mat. treća brojka iza decimalne oznake, treća decimala". So "dva cijela pet stotinki" is 2.05.

joiner.source: CLDR RBNF hr: "dvadeset i jedan"; Wiktionary (en), "pol": "tri i pol mjeseca", "three and a half months".

decimal_marker.source: CLDR RBNF hr: "x.x: << zarez >>;". Croatian also reads the whole part with cijela, cijele or cijelih: a paraphrase, with no read source.

minus_idioms.source: This lexicon lists no Croatian idiom that puts "minus" before a positive number.

article_one.source: Croatian has no article; "jedan" is a numeral.

of.source: Croatian marks the counted noun by case, with no "of" word.

fraction_of.source: Croatian marks the counted noun by case, with no "of" word.

vague_clitic.source: hr.wikipedia, "Enklitika" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/follow-up-prs/hr-nekoliko/sources/hr-wp-Enklitika.wikitext), wikitext list of the clitics of standard Croatian: "''biti'' – ''sam, si, je, smo, ste, su''"; "''htjeti'' – ''ću, ćeš, će, ćemo, ćete, će ''"; "aorista glagola ''biti'' – ''bih, bi, bi, bismo, biste, bi''"; and "nenaglašene riječi teže drugome mjestu u indoeuropskim rečenicama". So "nekoliko je tisuća puta dalje" (hr.wikipedia, "Amaterska astronomija", knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/follow-up-prs/hr-nekoliko/sources/hr-wp-Amaterska_astronomija.wikitext) holds the clitic between the vague word and the scale word. The scale word after the clitic may also be a singular form ("Puno je milijun eura"): the reading follows the genitive plural of the vague word and ignores the case of the scale word.

denominator_particle.source: Croatian has no particle like Portuguese "avos".

class_noun.source: Croatian names no digit class with a singular noun after a collective.

half_unit.source: Wiktionary (en), "pola": "pola sata", "half an hour": the half is its own word before the unit, read by the half role.

abbreviation.source: No Croatian number word in this lexicon is also an abbreviation with a period.

lone_decimal_mark.source: CLDR common/main/hr.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae): the decimal symbol is a comma; a comma before the first digit marks decimals.

range_cue.source: Wiktionary (en), "između": "between"; "i" joins the two limits, so it ends the first number.
